exclude: the processor port's two registers, not memory
the KERNAL's IRQ, BRK and NMI vectors, the machine's: ldr_reset_machine writes them from ldr_vectors
runtime: the text screen and its sprite pointers, written by the loader's side prompt and by the menu
RAM nothing writes: the alternating $FF $FF $00 $00 pattern it powers up with; the KERNAL ROM covers it whenever the loader runs
the processor's NMI, reset and IRQ vectors in the RAM under the KERNAL: $FFFA-$FFFB hold $0906, ldr_nmi; the rest is the power-on pattern
13 parts: The menu, the players and the medals, Fencing, The champion ceremony and others
elsewhere: 13 parts: The menu, the players and the medals, Fencing, The champion ceremony and others

comments.text: The unpacker's destination pointer, low byte first ($10-$11).
The high byte of ldr_dest.
The unpacker's source pointer, low byte first ($12-$13).
The high byte of ldr_src.
The file number ldr_file_offset was given.
The offset of the file's record in ldr_files, the file number times 12.
The side of the disk in the drive, from ldr_check_side: 1, 2, 4 for the first game's disk, or 0.
The third byte of the command ldr_command sends (X: a track, or a file's letter).
The fourth byte of the command ldr_command sends (Y: a sector).
The second byte of every command ldr_command sends; nothing in the loader sets it, so it goes as whatever is there.
The byte ldr_send_byte is shifting out, two bits a round.
Where ldr_load_by_name stores the file's next byte, low byte first ($22-$23): the load address the file starts with.
The high byte of ldr_load_ptr.
The byte ldr_get_byte shifts in, bit by bit, inverted.

The page of variables every part shares, which starts with the eight players' records, 32 bytes each at $0800, $0820 and on to $08E0: the name (10 characters) and a space, the country as "(USA)", the score as text (6 characters), the score as a number (3 bytes, low first, higher is better), the gold, silver and bronze counts, and the country's number. The last three bytes of each 32 hold other variables: the practice mark, the number of players and the event under way after the first record, the menu's state after the second ($083D says whether the menu must be loaded again), the resume address and the load flag after the third ($085D-$085F), the joysticks, the file letter and the Summer Games 1 switch after the fourth ($087D-$087F), the events chosen and the file in memory after the fifth ($089D-$089F), and the random numbers after the last ($08FD-$08FF). All zero in a snapshot taken before any names are typed.
The second byte of the first player's name, where the boot stage copied BASIC's program area from.
The first player's country as text, "(USA)", 5 bytes; the other records' at the same offset.
The first player's score as the event writes it, 6 characters, or FAULT.
The first player's score as a number, 3 bytes low first, higher being better; the results sort on it, and the champion's standings put the medal points here.
The first player's gold medals.
The first player's silver medals.
The first player's bronze medals.
The first player's country by number, row times 8 plus column of the flag picker.
Not zero while an event is being practised.
The number of players, 1 to 8.
The event under way, 0 to 15 in menu order.
The second player's record, laid out as the first's.
The second player's score as a number.
Bit 7 set when something has been loaded over the menu since it last ran; ldr_restart starts the menu without loading it while bit 7 is clear.
The menu option chosen last, where the menu's pointer starts.
The event picked last from a list.
The third player's record.
The high byte of the address the menu jumps to when it is started again ($085D is the low byte). ldr_nmi clears it when RUN/STOP is held with RESTORE, so that the menu starts from its top.
$36 while a file is loading, 0 once it has unpacked: ldr_run_file loads again when a load was cut short by RESTORE.
The fourth player's record.
The number of joysticks, 1 or 2, which the menu's option 5 switches and shows.
The one-letter name of the file being loaded, from offset 9 of its record, which ldr_load_by_name sends to the drive code.
Bit 7 set when the Summer Games 1 events are on (menu option 6).
The fifth player's record.
The events still to play in the competition, a bit each for events 0 to 7, the first in bit 7.
The same for events 8 to 15, the Summer Games 1 events.
The record offset (file number times 12) of the file loaded last, so ldr_run_file can skip a load when the file is still in memory.
The sixth player's record.
The seventh player's record.
The eighth player's record.
The random number generator's register, low byte.
The random number generator's register, high byte.
The counter the random number generator mixes in.
The loader's two entries, which every part calls at these fixed addresses: $0900 back to the menu (ldr_restart), $0903 load and start file X (ldr_run_file).

The NMI handler (RESTORE). With RUN/STOP held as well (bit 7 of row 7 read through CIA 1) it clears menu_resume_hi and goes back to the menu; alone it puts CIA 1's directions back and returns. While a file loads, ldr_load_file writes an RTI ($40) over its first byte, so RESTORE does nothing until the load is done, when ldr_unpack writes the SEI ($78) back.

Writes the 256 bytes at $0E00, the world records, to the disk: asks for side 1 until it is in (ldr_check_side, ldr_insert_side), then sends command 4 with track 18, sector 13 and the 256 bytes to the drive code.

Blanks the screen (ldr_blank) and asks the drive code for the side of the disk in the drive (command 3, track 18, sector 0), one byte; a "G" there, the Summer Games disk's mark, counts as side 4, and anything from 5 up as 0. Keeps the answer in $16.

Asks for another disk: fills colour RAM with cyan, writes "INSERT SUMMER GAMES II SIDE n" on line 6 and "THEN PRESS JOYSTICK BUTTON" on line 8 of the screen at $0400 in white, patches the second I and the digit from the tables at $09C7 and $09CB indexed by the side wanted in Y (side 4 blanks the I, so the line reads SUMMER GAMES I SIDE 1), shows the text screen and waits for fire on either joystick.

The RTS that ends ldr_insert_side. The three bytes after it are the letter for the second I of the prompt, read at $09C7+Y: "I" for sides 1 and 2 at $09C8-$09C9, and a space at $09CB for side 4, the first game's disk.
The side digit of the prompt, read at $09CB+Y: "1" at $09CC for side 1, "2" at $09CD for side 2, "1" at $09CF for side 4 (the first game's only side used).
"INSERT SUMMER GAMES II SIDE 1", 29 characters in ASCII order, which the ROM's upper- and lower-case font shows as capitals.
"THEN PRESS JOYSTICK BUTTON" and three spaces, the prompt's second line.
Notes the record offset in X as the file in memory, then falls into ldr_load_file.

Loads the file whose record offset is in $15: checks the side in the drive against the record's side mask (offset 0) and asks for the right one until they match, silences RESTORE (an RTI over ldr_nmi), starts CIA 2's timer A, loads the packed file by its letter (ldr_load_by_name), then unpacks it (ldr_unpack).

Unpacks the file just loaded, with the KERNAL and BASIC banked out ($01 = $34): reads from the record's load address (offset 1) and writes from its destination (offset 3) until the destination passes the record's end (offset 5). $BF n writes n zeros, $CF n b writes byte b n times, and any other byte is itself. Then clears loading_flag, banks the ROMs back in, gives RESTORE back to ldr_nmi and acknowledges CIA 2.
Stores A at the unpacker's destination pointer ($10) and moves it on.
Reads the next byte at the unpacker's source pointer ($12) and moves it on.
Back to the menu: resets the stack, puts the machine into a known state (ldr_reset_machine) and starts file 0, the menu, loading it first only when bit 7 of menu_stale is set.

Loads file number X (ldr_files) unless it is already in memory and its last load finished, then starts it: copies the record's entry address (offset 7) into the JMP at $0AF3, waits for the raster to wrap into a new frame, banks the KERNAL in ($01 = $36) and jumps.
The JMP's operand, which ldr_run_file overwrites with the entry of the file it starts.
The high byte of the JMP at $0AF3, the file's entry point.
Turns file number X into the offset of its record, X times 12, kept in $15 and returned in X; keeps the number in $14.
The end of ldr_file_offset: LDA #$FF and return.

Puts the machine in the state every part starts from: waits for raster line $FB, puts the KERNAL's IRQ, BRK and NMI vectors back from ldr_vectors, sets the processor port ($00 = $2F, $01 = $36), clears the sprite positions, the VIC's interrupts and the sprite colours, turns the sprites off, zeroes the SID's filter, sets the background colours, stops CIA 2's interrupts and lets CIA 1's timer A interrupt through, sets CIA 1 for the keyboard, silences the three SID voices and selects the video bank at $0000 ($DD00 bits 0 and 1 set).
The seven register values ldr_reset_machine writes to each SID voice: frequency and pulse width 0, control $08 (the test bit, which holds the oscillator silent), envelope 0.
The three colours ldr_reset_machine writes to $D021-$D023: cyan, red and white.
The KERNAL's IRQ, BRK and NMI vectors for $0314-$0319: $EA31, $FE66 and ldr_nmi.

Receives one byte from the drive code, two bits at a time on the serial bus: four times it waits for the clock line (bit 6 of $DD00) to go one way, takes the data line (bit 7) into $24, waits for it to go back and takes the next. Returns the byte inverted in A, since the lines read low for a 1.
The middle of ldr_get_byte: its second and third pairs of bits come through ldr_get_2bits.
Receives two bits on the serial bus, as ldr_get_byte does for its first two.
Blanks the screen ($D011 = $0B), turns the sprites off and waits for the raster to wrap past line 255 into a new frame.
Shows the text screen at $0400 in the ROM's upper- and lower-case font ($D018 = $17) and turns the display on ($D011 = $1B).
Sends the byte in A to the drive code, two bits at a time on the serial clock and data lines (four rounds), after waiting for the drive to say it is ready.

Sends the drive code a four-byte command: the command number in A, the byte in $1B, then X and Y. Commands used: 2 load a file by its letter in X, 3 read the side byte (track 18, sector 0), 4 write the 256 bytes that follow to the track and sector in X and Y.

The loader's file table: twenty records of twelve bytes. Offset 0 is the disk side as a mask (1 side 1, 2 side 2, 3 either, 4 the first Summer Games disk), 1-2 the address the packed file loads to, 3-4 where it unpacks to, 5-6 where the unpacking stops, 7-8 the entry point, and 9-11 the file's one-letter name three times. 0 "0" the menu ($0F00), 1 "1" the opening ceremony ($7600), 2 "2" the closing ceremony ($1000), 3 "3" the title ($9F40), 4 to 11 "4" to "9", "X" and "Y" the eight events in menu order, 12 to 16 and 19 "D", "E", "F" (twice), "H" and "K" the first game's events on its own disk, 17 and 18 "Z" with two entries, $17D0 and $17D3.
Offset 1 of every file record, read as $0C48,X: the load address, low byte.
Offset 2 of every file record: the load address, high byte.
Offset 3 of every file record: where it unpacks to, low byte.
Offset 4 of every file record: where it unpacks to, high byte.
Offset 5 of every file record: where unpacking stops, low byte.
Offset 6 of every file record: where unpacking stops, high byte.
Offset 7 of every file record: the entry point, low byte.
Offset 8 of every file record: the entry point, high byte.
Offset 9 of every file record: the file's one-letter name, sent to the drive code.
Turns the interrupts off and falls into ldr_load_by_name.

Loads one file: command 2 with the file's letter in X, then reads the load address and the file's bytes from the drive code into memory from there, with the ROMs banked out for each store. $AC is an escape: $AC $AC is one $AC, $AC $FF or $AC $F7 ends the file, and $AC with anything else is dropped.
RAM the loader leaves alone, holding the alternating $FF $00 pattern the C64's memory powers up with (and one stray $AD, $04 and $1F).

Bytes of the boot stage left behind: a JSR $C61A, a store of $78 $D8 $A2 into $C000-$C002, a JMP $C000, a JSR $FFE7 (CLALL) and the start of a load from $C6C6; nothing runs them once the loader is in place.

The world records, 256 bytes from track 18 sector 13 of side 1, which ldr_save_records writes back. Eight records of 20 bytes, one per event in menu order: the holder's name and a space (11 bytes), the score as text (6) and the score as a number (3 bytes, low first), which the menu compares with the winner's. On this disk they are another player's: NORMEN 16.95 m in Triple Jump, JOACHIM 0:27.9 in Rowing, FREDDY 100.87 m in Javelin, MARCO 82 in Equestrian, MARCO 2.30 m in High Jump, JOERG in Fencing, FREDDY 0:38.0 in Cycling, MARCO 2:03 in Kayaking.
The score of the first event's world record as a number, 3 bytes at offsets 17 to 19 of its record.
